CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR AUGUST 16, 2021 AT 4:30
P.M. WILL TAKE PLACE SOLELY BY
VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following
manner:
1. During the meeting, members of the public may provide live
public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to the start of public
comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda
item, please indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will
be handled according to the process posted on the agenda and as
specified in the City Council meeting policy). Public comments are
limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City Council may limit this
time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker
Card Help Line : If a public comment speaker needs assistance in
completing a speaker card, please
call the City Clerks Office at: (626) 744-4124. Help
line will open 30 minutes prior to the
posted start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after
the published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by
telephone. The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should
be used for the virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the
speaker.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may submit correspondence of any length prior to
the start of the meeting, at the following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council prior to the start
of the meeting, posted online, and made part of the legislative record
for the item.

Para facilitar la participacin del pblico en reuniones realizadas

1. Durante la reunin, los miembros del pblico pueden hacer

antes del inicio del comentario sobre el artculo que se est
tratando en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario pblico desea hablar sobre ms de un
artculo del orden del da, le solicitamos que lo indique en el
formulario en lnea (los oradores sobre artculos mltiples se
manejarn segn el proceso publicado en la agenda y lo especificado

comentarios pblicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el Alcalde y
el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.

de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pblica : Si
un orador de comentario pblico necesita asistencia para completar su
tarjeta, puede llamar a
la Oficina del
Secretario de la Ciudad al (626)
744-4124. La lnea de ayuda abrir 30 minutos antes del inicio de la
reunin.
Despus de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pblica, nase a la reunin
virtual a la hora de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro
dispositivo electrnico o por
telfono. Debe usar
el mismo nombre o nmero de telfono de la tarjeta de oratoria para la
reunin virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
orador.
Computadoras y dispositivos electrnicos pueden sumarse a la reunin en: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Nmero para ingresar a la reunin por telfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
reunin: 161 482 446
3. Los miembros del pblico pueden enviar correspondencia de
cualquier longitud antes del inicio de la reunin a la siguiente
direccin de correo electrnico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La correspondencia se enviar al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de
la reunin, se publicar en lnea, y se incorporar al registro
legislativo sobre el artculo.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  August 16, 2021 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:35 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Councilmember Masuda.

 ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson (Absent)
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Councilmember Williams introduced a District 2 student intern,
  David Kelly, a student at Marshal Fundamental High School who
Councilmember Madison  participated in the Project Talent Launch student intern program;
connected to the meeting at  and Stephen Lee, student at Polytechnic School, founder and CEO
4:40 p.m.  of Project Talent Launch (PTL), provided information on his
  organization and on the need for high school internships.

ORDINANCE  Conduct first reading of "AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  PASADENA AMENDING CHAPTER 17.50 OF TITLE 17 (ZONING
  CODE) OF THE PASADENA MUNICIPAL CODE TO INCREASE
  POTENTIAL CANNABIS RETAIL SITES, AND TO CORRECT
  DISTANCE SEPARATION BETWEEN CANNABIS LABS AND
  OTHER CANNABIS USES"

  The Mayor reported that the ordinance regarding cannabis retail
  sites is being held and will not be considered.

SPECIAL ITEM  COVID-19 UPDATE FROM DR. YING-YING GOH, PUBLIC
  HEALTH OFFICER

  Dr. Ying-Ying Goh, Director of Public Health/Public Health Officer,
  provided in oral update related to COVID-19, including information
  on confirmed COVID-19 cases in the US, California, and Pasadena.
  She also spoke on COVID-19 vaccination clinics in the City, the
  status of a third dose of COVID-19 vaccination, State Public Health
  Officer orders that affect the City; and responded to questions. Dr.

Council Minutes  08/16/2021
   Lori Morgan, CEO of Huntington Hospital, provided an update on
  COVID-19 patients admitted to the hospital and in the Intensive
  Care Unit, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy expressed appreciation to Dr. Goh, staff,
  Jana West, Patrice Marshall McKenzie and Luke Walker, for all their
  help with hosting a COVID-19 vaccination clinic at Luke Walker's
  Barber & Beauty shop in Pasadena.

  Councilmember Madison asked staff to provide data on California
  Counties' vaccination rates.

  Councilmember Williams requested that staff provide information
  on hospitalization rates, the number of people who tested positive
  for COVID-19 and developed COVID-19, the percentage that ended
  up in the hospital, and a comparison of the data from January and
  February of 2021 to the current surge.

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided information on the City's
  COVID-19 safety protocols for employees in the office; and
  responded to questions

  Mayor Gordo asked staff to monitor closely the number of COVI D-
  19 positive cases of students in the Pasadena Unified School
  District. He also asked staff to anticipate and prepare for the need
  to administer additional COVID-19 vaccines for boosters and young
  children. Mayor Gordo spoke on the need to support the City's
  business community and protect the public by incentivizing
  vaccination among the public industry work force in Pasadena. He
  asked staff to provide a recommendation of a voluntary incentive
  tool for local businesses to adopt a COVID-19 vaccination policy
  similar to that in the public sector (i.e. mandatory vaccination,
  regular testing) by recognizing businesses with a private logo/sign
  that would indicate a particular business in the City has adopted a
  mandatory COVID-19 vaccination/testing policy.

  Councilmembers Rivas, Hampton and Madison spoke in favor of
  staff developing a voluntary incentive tool for local businesses that
  adopt a COVID-19 vaccination/testing policy. Councilmember
  Madison advocated for the City to adopt a similar ordinance to that
  of the City of Los Angeles and County of Los Angeles that are
  considering requiring vaccinations for patrons in order to be allowed
  into certain businesses.

  Councilmember Kennedy recommended that the concept of
  developing a voluntary incentive tool for local businesses should be
  agendized at a future City Council committee meeting; and request
  input from the Pasadena Chamber of Commerce.

Council Minutes  2  08/16/2021
   Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus of
  the City Council, the information was received and filed.

PUBLIC COMMENT  The following individuals spoke on affordable housing in Northwest
  Pasadena; expressed concerns with sidewalk conditions, and
  empty lots with trash along North Fair Oaks Avenue, and/or
  advocated for the City Council to move forward with the rezoning
  of land owned by churches and other religious organizations to
  allow for the building and providing of affordable housing:

  Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community
  Happen
  Karen Newe, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Hampton asked staff to provide an update on
  sidewalk repairs that are scheduled along Fair Oaks Avenue in
  Pasadena. In response, City Manager Mermell responded that
  staff will bring forward a contract for City Council to approve in
  September for miscellaneous concrete repair to address
  outstanding concrete repairs in the City.

  The following individuals advocated for the City Council to
  agendize the City's investigating process of officer involved
  shootings, the termination of Pasadena Police Chief Perez,
  Officers Dumaguindin, Serrano, Mulrooney, and City Manager
  Steve Mermell, spoke on controversial incidents involving
  Pasadena police officers, and expressed concerns with the
  Pasadena Police Department, and the Department's policing
  policies:

  Jasmine Richards Abdullah, representing Black Lives Matter
  Pasadena
  Adriana Bautista, Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousos, representing Making Housing and
  Community Happen
  Evie, Pasadena resident
  Jason Reedy, Los Angeles resident
  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident
  Oldem Dendam, Pasadena resident
  Tess Posso, La Crescenta resident
  Caleb, El Monte resident

  Councilmember Hampton reiterated his request that a discussion
  on a policy that requires internal investigations to be completed
  within three months be agendized at a future City Council meeting.
  Mayor Gordo responded that the City Attorney will provide a memo
  to the City Council on the matter.

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's inquiry related to staff's
  actions to expedite the results of the District Attorney's Office
  investigation on the officer involved shooting of Anthony McClain,

Council Minutes  3  08/16/2021
   Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor, stated that
  she has made several calls to the District Attorney's Office and
  spoke to a representative who stated that the report is in progress
  and is not able to provide a specific time frame on when the
  investigation will be complete.

  Councilmember Kennedy asked Mayor Gordo and staff to write a
  letter to the District Attorney's Office voicing the concerns of the
  community related to the length of time of the investigation process
  and request that the investigation of the officer involved shooting
  of Anthony McClain be expedited.

  In response, Mayor Gordo stated he will work with the City Attorney
  and City Manager to generate correspondence to the District
  Attorney's Office requesting an update on the matter.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Madison
  explained that he is not logged off during public comment session;
  and stated that he is not in support of comments made by the public
  speakers to terminate City Manager Steve Mermell or Police Chief
  Perez.

  Mayor Gordo stated the following for the record, "The City Manager
  [Steve Mermell] is here in the Council Chambers with
  Councilmember Rivas and Councilmember Williams, and City
  Clerk [Mark Jomsky] and City Attorney [Michele Beal Bagneris]."

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Kennedy reported
  that Donald R. Matthews, member of the Community Police
  Oversight Commission, is a respected member of the Pasadena
  community and is the only African American male on the
  Commission.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Kennedy stated
  the following for the record: "I want to be crystal clear for the record,
  only for the record, I have no authority to fire any officer. Solely the
  City Manager without five votes ... it takes five votes to fire the City
  Manager. It is not reposed in the City Council to fire any employee
  other than the three employees, and a possible fourth employee.
  That would be the City Prosecutor, the City Attorney, those could
  be separate individuals, the City Clerk and the City Manager. And
  no matter how much the speaker implores that John Kennedy
  somehow has the power to do what he suggests, is simply isn't
  true. Thank you Mayor."

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:

  Section 15061 (b)(3), the General Rule that CEQA only applies to

  (2) In accordance with California Government Code Section
  85702.5, consider whether to enact local regulations governing
  campaign contribution limits for the City of Pasadena, and direct the
  City Attorney to prepare an ordinance within 60 days to codify the
  direction of the City Council in the Pasadena Municipal Code.

  Mayor Gordo presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item and
  responded to questions. City Clerk Jomsky and City Attorney
  Bagneris provided information on the City's Tax Payer Protection
  Act (TPA), and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated and asked staff to determine
  the City's ability to limit the amount of campaign contributions from
  organized labor entities.

  Councilmember Williams advocated to include other developers
  and other entitlements (i.e. cannabis) on campaign contribution
  limitations.

  City Attorney Bagneris summarized the direction to staff, which is
  for staff to return with an ordinance that provides that there will be
  no dollar limits on local campaign finance contributions, which is
  consistent with what has existed historically in Pasadena prior to
  AB 571, and provide information in the City Manager's Newsletter
  on the City's ability to further limit campaign contributions by groups
  or individuals who do business with the City.

  Councilmember Rivas spoke in opposition to the staff
  recommendation; expressed concerns with large campaign
  contributions and how they are perceived by the public and voiced
  support for Assembly Bill 571 default limit contributions.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Kennedy,
  seconded by Councilmember Masuda, to approve the Mayor's and
  Ad Hoc Committee recommendations to prepare an ordinance that
  provides that there will be no dollar limits on local campaign finance
  contributions, which is consistent with what has existed historically
  in Pasadena prior to AB 571:
